sentences.text:
As per the terms of settlement, petitioner no.1 is to pay to respondent no.2 a sum of Rs.3 Lacs as full and final settlement of all her claims, including maintenance (past, present and future),
permanent alimony, stridhan, in three instalments of Rs.1 Lac each.
6. Learned counsel jointly submit that a sum of Rs.2 Lacs has already been remitted to respondent no.2 in the interregnum.
Learned counsel for respondent no.2 affirms the submissions made by learned counsel for the petitioners.
The remaining balance of Rs.1 Lac has been tendered today to respondent no.2 in Court vide Demand Draft bearing No.043347 dated 11.09.2023 drawn on Union Bank of India, Barwala Branch, Delhi.

The receipt whereof is acknowledged by respondent no.2,
who is present in person.
7. In accordance with the terms of settlement, the parties have dissolved their marriage by way of decree of divorce under the provisions of Section 13B of HMA, 1955.

Photocopy of the decree dated 28.04.2023 is placed on record at page 152 at Annexure C.
8.
An affidavit of respondent no.2 deposing her "no objection" has also been placed on record at page 193 of the present petition.
9. This Court has interacted with respondent no.2, who affirms the terms of settlement.
She also confirms the receipt of Rs.3 Lacs as full This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 20/10/2023 at 22:16:08 and final settlement and submits that she has no objection in case the aforesaid FIR is quashed.
10.
This Court has perused the terms of settlement agreement and they appear to be lawful.
The parties are bound by the terms of the settlement.

11. After observing that the disputes are arising from matrimonial ties, this Court is of the considered opinion that no purpose would be served in continuing with the FIR in question and the further criminal proceedings and it would be in the interest of justice as also of the parties and the society that quietus is put to such disputes.
12.
Accordingly, FIR No. 167/2016 dated 18.01.2016 under Sections 498A/406/34, IPC, registered at Police Station Mehrauli and the proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
13. The petition stands disposed of.
TUSHAR RAO GEDELA, J OCTOBER 17, 2023 Aj
